# Skel

> Skel is your own team of coding agents, working while you're away. You brief a lead agent in the harness you already use. It writes the tasks and hands each one to a builder, and a fresh reviewer on another model checks every pull request. The team works on your own server, so you can close the laptop. You decide what merges. Open source.

Status: early. Earlier versions ran tasks to pull requests through phases, roles and gates defined as files; the current rewrite, started in November 2026, organises agents as a small team instead. No public release yet. Updates: https://skel.run/#updates

## The team

- The lead: your agent, in your harness, on your server. It turns what you say into tasks (GitHub issues) and starts a thread on each.
- Builders: one per task, each in its own clone, branch and sandbox. A builder stays on the thread until the pull request merges.
- Reviewers: a fresh one every round, on another model than the builder (Codex by default), looking for what the builder missed.
- You: say what you want, answer questions, and decide what merges.

## What you hand off

- Task to merged pull request, while you're away
- Many tasks at once, across repositories
- Every pull request reviewed by a fresh agent; the verdict is a GitHub review and a `skel/review` status check
- CI failures and pull request comments wake the builder again
- It asks you only when it needs you: a builder's question, a review that won't settle, or a pull request that is approved and green
- You decide what merges

## Open

- Harness: Claude Code today, with Codex as reviewer. Codex, opencode and pi as harnesses next.
- Models: builder on one, reviewer on another, on the subscriptions you already pay for. Skel never resells model usage.
- Server: a Linux machine you control, over SSH, or a Sprite on Fly.io that Skel creates for you and that sleeps when there's no work.
- Isolation: a sandbox per agent; your checkouts are never touched; your home folder and credentials are hidden; agents never see your GitHub token.
- Free and open source.

## Settings example

```yaml
# ~/.config/skel/config.yaml
harness: claude
builder:  { model: opus }
reviewer: { harness: codex }
max_rounds: 3

# skel.yaml in a repository
setup: [bun install]
test: [bun test]
```
